findings.title: A dummy TOTP value lets backup-code login bypass the password
findings.body: Password verification above this branch runs only when credentials.totpCode is empty. A caller can therefore submit an account's email, a valid backupCode, and any nonempty totpCode (for example, "x") without supplying the password. This new branch accepts the backup code and never validates the supplied TOTP, so authentication succeeds with only the recovery code instead of both authentication factors. Ensure password authentication for CAL accounts cannot be skipped by supplying an unverified TOTP alongside a backup code.

findings.title: Backup-code consumption is not atomic
findings.body: The backup-code list is read before validation and then overwritten with an update conditioned only on the user ID. Two concurrent login requests can read the same list, validate the same code, and both successfully authenticate, violating the single-use guarantee. Concurrent requests using different codes can also overwrite each other's removals, making a consumed code usable again. Consume codes atomically, such as through a conditional update against the previously read ciphertext whose success is checked before granting access.

findings.title: Identity-provider users cannot access backup-code recovery
findings.body: When totpEmail is present after Google or SAML authentication, the page renders ExternalTotpFooter instead of TwoFactorFooter. Only TwoFactorFooter exposes the Lost access button, so these users can never reach the backup-code input. This affects accounts that generated backup codes while using CAL authentication and subsequently switched to an identity provider: the authentication callbacks retain their enabled 2FA and backup codes. The server also rejects a third-party account's backup-only submission because its identity-provider guards require totpCode. Provide a recovery route for this flow and make the server accept its backup-code authentication; otherwise users with valid saved codes remain locked out after losing their authenticator.
